notes: Surface molten for a few million years after the Moon-forming impact (Elkins-Tanton 2008).

Map shows an ocean world with placeholder islands; real positions unknown. Liquid oceans by ~4.4 Ga (Jack Hills zircons; Wilde 2001). Sun ~25-30% dimmer; warmth from CO2 and methane. Whether early oceans were temperate or hot is debated.
Huronian glaciations; map shows global ice with geography unknown. Ice reached low latitudes at least once (~2.4-2.2 Ga). Follows the Great Oxidation Event.
Few or no glacial deposits for ~1.5 Gyr (the 'boring billion'). Probably little or no ice. Temperatures poorly constrained.
Sturtian glaciation. Ice to the equator (Hoffman 2017).
Marinoan glaciation. Ice to the equator (Hoffman 2017).
Ediacaran. Cap carbonates suggest a brief hot greenhouse after the Marinoan. Short regional Gaskiers glaciation ~580 Ma.
Warm and largely ice-free. Early Cambrian tropical seas ~30-38 C in models (Wong Hearing 2021).
Hirnantian glaciation over Gondwana. End-Ordovician extinction.
Mostly warm. Brief Late Devonian glaciations in South America.
Late Paleozoic Ice Age. Ice sheets across southern Gondwana.
Little or no polar ice. Peaks at the end-Permian (~252 Ma; tropical seas ~40 C; Sun 2012) and the mid-Cretaceous and Early Eocene.
Antarctic ice sheet from 34 Ma. Northern ice sheets from ~2.7 Ma.

Pangaea Proxima (Scotese; called Pangea Ultima in Farnsworth 2023). One of several competing scenarios; chosen here. Map from a HadCM3L run at 2x CO2 and a 2.5% brighter Sun. Much of the interior too hot for mammals (Farnsworth 2023).
Brightening Sun drives off the oceans. Timing estimates vary.
Oceans gone. Surface hot and dry; plate tectonics likely slowed or stopped. Geography unknown.
Sun leaves the main sequence in ~5 Gyr and reaches the red giant tip at ~7.6 Gyr (Schroder & Smith 2008).
